title: LBJ: The Play by Sunny Zimmerman at Paradise Factory #lbjtheplay #par...
transcript: A history lesson on the 1960s goes completely awry in this messy but thought provoking comedy. We, the audience, are fifth graders, and our teacher has hired a few local actors to provide us a history lesson as L.B.J. and J.F.K. Things immediately go off the rails, with the presentation not only being historically inaccurate, but incredibly inappropriate for fifth graders. The premise is really funny, and all of the aspects of the show that ground it in the world of a fifth grade classroom are hilarious. However, it meanders too much, getting bogged down with the interpersonal issues between the actors and providing no clear narrative direction for a lot of the piece. Eventually, it lands the plane, invoking some interesting questions about masculinity and the sticky nature of aspiring to it. I liked the ending, though it felt shoehorned in after the chaotic and seemingly unrelated 90 minutes that preceded it. While the show already packs plenty of funny moments, maybe some workshopping to focus and hone in on the themes would bring it more clarity and more comedy.
